t.5.41.1: Then Hanumān, having slain the Kiṃkaras, became absorbed in thought: "The grove has been broken by me, but the temple-palace has not been destroyed; therefore I shall now likewise demolish this palace too."
t.5.41.2: Having thus reflected in his mind, Hanumān, displaying his strength, leapt up to the temple-palace, lofty like a peak of Meru; Hanumān, foremost of monkeys, son of the Wind, ascended it.
t.5.41.3: Having assailed the lofty temple-palace, the unassailable Hanūmān, blazing with splendour, became like the Pāriyātra mountain.
t.5.41.4: Then Hanumān, the son of the Wind, became huge of body and boldly slapped his arms, filling Laṅkā with the sound.
t.5.41.5: At the mighty, ear-shattering sound of his slapping of his arms, birds fell from the sky, and he loudly proclaimed this:
t.5.41.6: Victorious is Rāma of surpassing strength, and Lakṣmaṇa of mighty strength; victorious is King Sugrīva, protected by Rāghava.
t.5.41.7: I am the servant of Rāma, lord of Kosala, whose deeds are accomplished without strain; I am Hanumān, son of Māruta, slayer of the hosts of the enemy.
t.5.41.8: Not even a thousand Rāvaṇas could be a match for me in battle as I strike with rocks and with trees by the thousands.
t.5.41.9: Having harassed the city of Laṅkā and having saluted Maithilī, I shall depart with my purpose accomplished, while all the Rākṣasas look on.
t.5.41.11: At that mighty sound a hundred guardians of the sanctuary came forth, seizing weapons of many kinds, spears, swords and battle-axes. Hurling them, those huge-bodied ones surrounded Māruti.
t.5.41.12: Having surrounded the best of monkeys, that host of Rākṣasas shone like a vast and mighty whirlpool in the waters of the Gaṅgā.
t.5.41.10: Having spoken thus to those stationed at the sanctuary, the bull among monkeys, standing atop the lofty edifice, roared with a terrible, resounding cry, striking fear into the rākṣasas.
t.5.41.13: Then the son of the Wind, enraged, assumed a terrible form.
t.5.41.15: Having slain a hundred rākṣasas, as Indra slew the asuras with his thunderbolt, the glorious one, stationed in the sky, spoke these words.
t.5.41.14: Then the great Hanumān, the mighty son of Māruta, forcefully uprooted a gold-adorned pillar of that palace and whirled that hundred-edged pillar around.
t.5.41.16: Thousands of mighty, great-souled lords of the vānaras like me, who are obedient to the will of Sugrīva, have been sent forth.
t.5.41.17: Sugrīva, the destroyer of you all, will come with hundreds, with hundreds of thousands, with tens of thousands, and even with tens of millions.
t.5.41.18: This city of Laṅkā is as good as gone, and so are you, and so is Rāvaṇa, since enmity has been bound fast with the great-souled lord of the Ikṣvākus.
